findings.title: The array_agg FILTER is named as the reconciliation safety boundary in three places, but removing it alone is caught by nothing — the real guard is src/lib/agents/operator/turns.ts:58
findings.reason: M6 removed the FILTER and all 19 live-DB cases stayed green, including the operator case that deviations D1 says exists to pin exactly this. M8 shows the invariant only bites when the callee guard at turns.ts:58 also falls. The production comment (:135-136), docs/context/core-platform-runtime.md:9 and deviations D1 therefore credit a redundant pre-filter as the safety boundary, and D1 justifies weakening the operator assertion on a premise that does not hold.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The survivor is semantically meaningful (it changes which rows reach reconcileTurnForFailedOutbox and adds one SELECT per terminalized row), but it is PROVEN behaviour-preserving for correctness by turns.ts:58, so the inventory row is equivalent and this is filed as a docs/oracle finding rather than a P0.

findings.title: The 2-minute terminal window is smaller than the worst-case claim-to-markDispatched gap the dispatch path itself can produce, so a still-dispatching row on any topic can now be terminalized
findings.reason: Topic groups dispatch serially (:441-455), each bounded by OUTBOX_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_MS default 10s (:54), across up to 37 registered topics — roughly 6 minutes worst case. The overlap guard (:84) supersedes a cycle after 60s and the superseding cycle runs the watchdog first, so a third cycle can terminalize rows the first cycle claimed and has not yet dispatched. markDispatched (:244) is status-scoped to dispatching and then writes nothing SILENTLY while addBulk may have succeeded. The same race already existed on arm 3 for retryable rows where the cost is an idempotent duplicate; #1378 makes the consequence TERMINAL and generalizes it from agent_turn to every topic. Raised for adjudication only — the intake non_goals forbid changing the window in this run.

findings.title: The terminal path the diff adds for ~30 of 37 topics has no alert half at all, and it removes the outbox_stale_dispatching signal those rows used to raise
findings.reason: checkFailedOutboxByTopic is a CLOSED 7-topic allowlist; the Job-failure sink fires only on BullMQ terminal failed events, which a watchdog terminalization never produces; and docs/runbooks/beta-launch-alerting.md:346-349 still scopes the companion signal to a long-dispatched row, with no rule row added or amended for the long-dispatching class. Before #1378 such a row raised outbox_stale_dispatching (checks.ts:166, level error) permanently — the change trades a loud misleading signal for silence on the non-allowlisted topics. The intake acknowledgement is accurate in what it says but omits that an existing signal is removed, frames the clearing as a benefit in user_visible_behavior #3, and names a symbol that does not exist. ArchivalPoller.ts:78 retains failed rows 90 days, so the row stays auditable in /admin/jobs but never pages.

findings.title: The claimed gate evidence was recorded 14 minutes before HEAD was committed and is pinned to the base SHA
findings.reason: gate-status.json timestamp 1789945687 = 2026-09-20T23:08:07Z with passed:false; .feature/state.json pins headSha to 650f625e788d1a87a770c77d40ae8a2d41730982 (the base) with intakeSha256 empty and phase executing; f9aa7d350 and 3bc5f1a31 were both committed at 2026-09-20T23:22:31Z; and surfaceAmendmentLog[1] — the arch-review-log row that ci:merge-ledger requires — is stamped 23:18:12Z, after the gate recorded merge-ledger PASS. The claim "15,299 tests pass; lint, typecheck and 26 ci:* audits green" therefore describes a tree that is not 3bc5f1a31, and the gate must be re-run against current HEAD as the last serialized step.

findings.title: A tautological assertion compares two file-local literals, while the assertion that would pin the suite premise is absent
findings.reason: expect(DISPATCHING_RECLAIM_TEXT).not.toBe(GENERIC_RECLAIM_TEXT) compares two string constants declared at :68 and :72 of the same file and can never fail on any implementation. Behavioural replacement: expect(PROBE_TOPIC).not.toBe(QUEUE_NAMES.AGENT_TURN), which pins the premise the whole topic-blindness acceptance rests on and is currently stated only in a comment.
